questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the economy of Karnataka?

options.A: Only the agricultural production within the State
options.B: The system of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services within the State
options.C: Only the industrial output of the State
options.D: Only the service sector activities in the State

questions.explanation: The economy of Karnataka is the system of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services within the State, covering agriculture, industry, services, trade, infrastructure and public administration.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP)?

options.A: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of Karnataka during a given accounting period
options.B: The total income earned by residents of Karnataka
options.C: The total value of exports from Karnataka
options.D: The total savings of the State government

questions.explanation: GSDP is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of Karnataka during a given accounting period, usually one financial year.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What does GSDP measure?

options.A: The size and overall economic output of Karnataka's economy
options.B: The distribution of income among households
options.C: The level of unemployment in the State
options.D: The rate of inflation in the State

questions.explanation: GSDP measures the size and overall economic output of Karnataka's economy; it is the State-level counterpart of India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between GDP and GSDP?

options.A: GDP measures production within the entire country, whereas GSDP measures production within one State's geographical boundaries
options.B: GSDP measures production within the entire country, whereas GDP measures production within one State
options.C: There is no difference between GDP and GSDP
options.D: GDP is used only for Karnataka and GSDP is used only for India

questions.explanation: GDP measures the value of final production within the entire country, whereas GSDP measures the value of final production within one State's geographical boundaries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Gross Value Added (GVA)?

options.A: The value of output produced by an economic activity minus the value of intermediate goods and services consumed in production
options.B: The total value of all goods and services produced in the economy
options.C: The total tax revenue collected by the government
options.D: The total consumption expenditure of households

questions.explanation: GVA is the value of output produced by an economic activity minus the value of intermediate goods and services consumed in production. It measures the value added by producers.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How is GSDP at market prices related to GVA?

options.A: GSDP at market prices is obtained by adding taxes on products and subtracting subsidies on products from the sum of GVA at basic prices
options.B: GSDP at market prices is exactly equal to GVA at basic prices
options.C: GSDP at market prices is obtained by subtracting taxes and adding subsidies to GVA
options.D: GSDP at market prices is always lower than GVA at basic prices

questions.explanation: Broadly, GSDP at market prices is obtained by adding taxes on products and subtracting subsidies on products from the sum of Gross Value Added at basic prices.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Net State Domestic Product (NSDP)?

options.A: The net value of goods and services produced within the State after deducting Consumption of Fixed Capital from GSDP
options.B: The total value of goods and services produced within the State without any deductions
options.C: The total income of the State government
options.D: The total value of exports minus imports

questions.explanation: NSDP is the net value of goods and services produced within the State after deducting Consumption of Fixed Capital (depreciation) from GSDP.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Consumption of Fixed Capital (CFC)?

options.A: The estimated value of fixed assets used up or worn out during production in an accounting period
options.B: The total consumption expenditure of households
options.C: The total capital expenditure of the government
options.D: The total fixed investment in the economy

questions.explanation: CFC is the estimated value of fixed assets used up or worn out during production in an accounting period; it is commonly described as depreciation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is per-capita income in a State?

options.A: The average income per person, calculated by dividing the State's NSDP at current prices by its estimated mid-year population
options.B: The total income of the State divided by the number of districts
options.C: The total income of the State divided by the number of workers
options.D: The total income of the State divided by the number of households

questions.explanation: Per-capita income is the average income per person, calculated by dividing the State's Net State Domestic Product (NSDP) at current prices by its estimated mid-year population.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Does per-capita income show how income is distributed among individuals or households?

options.A: Yes, it perfectly shows income distribution
options.B: No, it is an arithmetic average and does not show how income is distributed among individuals or households
options.C: Yes, it shows the median income of households
options.D: Yes, it shows the income of the poorest section

questions.explanation: Per-capita income is an arithmetic average and does not show how income is distributed among individuals or households.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is economic growth?

options.A: An increase in the real output of goods and services produced by an economy over time, generally measured by the growth rate of GDP or GSDP at constant prices
options.B: An increase in the price level of goods and services over time
options.C: An increase in the population of the economy over time
options.D: An increase in the money supply in the economy over time

questions.explanation: Economic growth is an increase in the real output of goods and services produced by an economy over time, generally measured by the growth rate of GDP or GSDP at constant prices.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between current prices and constant prices?

options.A: Current prices use prices prevailing in the year being measured and include inflation, while constant prices use prices of a fixed base year to remove the effect of price changes
options.B: Current prices use prices of a fixed base year, while constant prices use prices prevailing in the year being measured
options.C: Current prices and constant prices are the same
options.D: Current prices are used only for agriculture, while constant prices are used only for industry

questions.explanation: Current prices use the prices prevailing in the year being measured and therefore include the effect of inflation. Constant prices use prices of a fixed base year to remove the effect of price changes and measure real growth.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why are constant-price estimates important?

options.A: They help determine whether actual production has increased, rather than merely showing an increase caused by inflation
options.B: They help determine the rate of inflation in the economy
options.C: They help determine the population growth rate
options.D: They help determine the money supply in the economy

questions.explanation: Constant-price estimates help determine whether actual production has increased, rather than merely showing an increase caused by inflation.

options.B: The final estimate of economic performance after all data are available
options.C: An estimate prepared by the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: An estimate prepared by the Planning Commission

questions.explanation: An Advance Estimate is an early estimate of economic performance prepared before all final data become available; it may be revised when more complete information is received.

questions.explanation: A First Revised Estimate is an updated estimate prepared after additional data become available; it can differ from the earlier advance estimate.

options.B: The total number of sectors in the economy
options.C: The total number of industries in the economy
options.D: The total number of workers in each sector

questions.explanation: Sectoral composition refers to the proportion of total economic output or value added contributed by different sectors, such as primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

questions.explanation: The three broad sectors are the primary sector, which extracts or produces natural resources; the secondary sector, which processes raw materials and manufactures goods; and the tertiary sector, which provides services.

options.A: Manufacturing was 11.33%, construction was 5.88% and electricity, gas, water supply and remediation services was 1.49% of GSVA at current prices
options.B: Manufacturing was 5.88%, construction was 11.33% and utilities was 1.49% of GSVA at current prices
options.C: Manufacturing was 1.49%, construction was 5.88% and utilities was 11.33% of GSVA at current prices
options.D: Manufacturing was 18.71%, construction was 5.88% and utilities was 1.49% of GSVA at current prices

questions.explanation: In 2025-26, manufacturing's share was 11.33 per cent, construction's share was 5.88 per cent, and electricity, gas, water supply and remediation services' share was 1.49 per cent of Karnataka's GSVA at current prices.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following correctly ranks the service sub-sectors by their share in Karnataka's GSVA in 2025-26 from highest to lowest?

options.A: Real estate, ownership of dwellings and professional services (41.28%) > Trade and repair services (8.93%) > Other services (6.31%) > Transport, storage, communication and broadcasting (4.57%) > Public administration (2.26%)
options.B: Trade and repair services (8.93%) > Real estate, ownership of dwellings and professional services (41.28%) > Public administration (2.26%) > Other services (6.31%) > Transport (4.57%)
options.C: Public administration (2.26%) > Transport (4.57%) > Other services (6.31%) > Trade and repair services (8.93%) > Real estate (41.28%)
options.D: Other services (6.31%) > Public administration (2.26%) > Transport (4.57%) > Trade and repair services (8.93%) > Real estate (41.28%)

questions.explanation: The correct ranking from highest to lowest is: Real estate, ownership of dwellings and professional services (41.28%) > Trade and repair services (8.93%) > Other services (6.31%) > Transport, storage, communication and broadcasting (4.57%) > Public administration (2.26%).

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the scope of Karnataka's economy is correct?

options.A: It covers agriculture, industry, services, trade, infrastructure and public administration
options.B: It covers only agriculture
options.D: It covers only services

questions.explanation: The economy of Karnataka is the system of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services within the State, covering agriculture, industry, services, trade, infrastructure and public administration.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the per-capita income gap between Bengaluru Urban and Kalaburagi division in 2024-25 is correct?

options.A: Bengaluru Urban's per-capita income (₹8,55,960) was much higher than Kalaburagi division's (₹1,89,938), highlighting regional disparity
options.B: Kalaburagi division's per-capita income was higher than Bengaluru Urban's
options.D: Kalaburagi division had the highest per-capita income in the State

questions.explanation: Bengaluru Urban recorded the highest per-capita income at ₹8,55,960 in 2024-25, while Kalaburagi division recorded the lowest at ₹1,89,938, highlighting significant regional disparity in Karnataka's economy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's economy is NOT correct?

options.A: Karnataka's economy is entirely dependent on agriculture with no significant services sector
options.B: Karnataka has a strong services and IT base
options.D: Karnataka has a strong start-up and innovation ecosystem

questions.explanation: Karnataka's economy is not entirely dependent on agriculture; it has a strong services and IT base, established manufacturing clusters, a skilled workforce, a strong start-up and innovation ecosystem, agricultural and horticultural diversity, major ports and transport links, and significant potential in renewable energy, tourism and exports.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's primary sector is NOT correct?

options.A: The primary sector includes manufacturing and construction
options.B: The primary sector includes agriculture and animal husbandry
options.C: The primary sector includes forestry and fishing
options.D: The primary sector includes mining and quarrying

questions.explanation: The primary sector does not include manufacturing and construction; these are part of the secondary sector. The primary sector includes agriculture, animal husbandry, forestry, fishing, mining and quarrying.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's secondary sector is NOT correct?

options.A: The secondary sector includes mining and quarrying
options.B: The secondary sector includes manufacturing
options.D: The secondary sector includes electricity, gas and water supply

questions.explanation: The secondary sector does not include mining and quarrying; mining and quarrying is part of the primary sector. The secondary sector includes manufacturing, construction, electricity, gas, water supply and related utilities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's tertiary sector is NOT correct?

options.A: The tertiary sector includes manufacturing and construction
options.B: The tertiary sector includes trade and transport
options.C: The tertiary sector includes banking and insurance
options.D: The tertiary sector includes education and healthcare

questions.explanation: The tertiary sector does not include manufacturing and construction; these are part of the secondary sector. The tertiary sector includes trade, transport, communication, banking, insurance, real estate, education, health, tourism, public administration and information technology services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about per-capita income is NOT correct?

options.A: Per-capita income shows how income is distributed among individuals or households
options.B: Per-capita income is an arithmetic average
options.C: Per-capita income is calculated using NSDP at current prices and estimated mid-year population
options.D: Per-capita income is the average income per person

questions.explanation: Per-capita income does not show how income is distributed among individuals or households; it is an arithmetic average. It is calculated by dividing NSDP at current prices by estimated mid-year population.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Advance Estimates is NOT correct?

options.A: Advance Estimates are final and never revised
options.B: Advance Estimates are prepared before all final data become available
options.C: Advance Estimates may be revised when more complete information is received
options.D: Advance Estimates are early estimates of economic performance

questions.explanation: Advance Estimates are not final and may be revised when more complete information is received. They are early estimates of economic performance prepared before all final data become available.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about First Revised Estimates is NOT correct?

options.A: First Revised Estimates are always identical to Advance Estimates
options.B: First Revised Estimates are updated estimates prepared after additional data become available
options.C: First Revised Estimates can differ from earlier advance estimates
options.D: First Revised Estimates are prepared after additional data become available

questions.explanation: First Revised Estimates are not always identical to Advance Estimates; they are updated estimates prepared after additional data become available and can differ from the earlier advance estimate.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the source of Karnataka's official domestic product estimates is correct?

options.A: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Government of Karnataka prepares the estimates
options.B: The Reserve Bank of India prepares the estimates
options.D: The Ministry of Finance, Government of India prepares the estimates

questions.explanation: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Government of Karnataka prepares the State's official domestic product estimates.
